Rashi on Pesachim 62a:10:1.hebrew: אלא פשיטא בטומאת גברי - שאפילו פסח, שלא הותר ליחיד טמא לשלח פסחו לעזרה לשחוט, הותר לציבור טמאין להביא פסחיהן בטומאה אם רובן טמאין. נמצא שהותרה מכלל איסורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:10:1.english: Rather, it is obvious [that it refers] to impurity of the people - For even the Paschal offering, which was not permitted for an impure individual to send his Paschal offering to the Temple Courtyard to be slaughtered, was permitted for an impure congregation to bring their Paschal offerings in [a state of] impurity if the majority of them are impure. Thus it is found that it was permitted from its general prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:10:2.hebrew: ערל וטמא משלחין קרבנותיהן - בעזרה, חוץ מפסח, דבעינן ראוי לאוכלו, שאכילת בעליו מעכבת בו, דכתיב: "לפי אכלו תכוסו":
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:10:2.english: An uncircumcised person and one who is impure send their offerings - [into] the Temple Courtyard, except for the Paschal lamb, for we require [one who is] fit to eat it, since the eating of its owner is essential to it, as it is written: "According to his eating shall you count."

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:12:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - לעולם בטומאת בשר, ומאי "אינו נוהג בכל הזבחים"? אין מנהגא בשאר זבחים שוה למנהגא בפסח. דאילו בשאר זבחים, לר' יהושע דאמר בכיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים דף עז.) "אם אין בשר אין דם" — אם בשר קיים לאכילת אדם או חלב קיים לאכילת מזבח, זורק את הדם; ואילו פסח, לא מהניא אכילת מזבח לזרוק דם עליה, אלא אם נשתייר כזית בשר, כדתנן בכיצד צולין:
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:12:1.english: And if you wish, say - Actually, [it is] regarding impurity of the meat. And what [is the meaning of] "it does not apply to all offerings"? The practice with other offerings is not the same as the practice with the Paschal lamb. For whereas with other offerings, according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who says in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (later, Pesachim 77a), "If there is no meat, there is no blood" — if meat remains for human consumption or fat remains for altar consumption, [the priest] sprinkles the blood; whereas [with] the Paschal lamb, altar consumption does not avail to sprinkle blood on its account unless an olive's bulk of meat remains, as we learned in the Mishnah in Keitzad Tzolin.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:14:1.hebrew: דנין דבר שלא הותר מכללו - ערלה במקום שאסרה, דהיינו בפסח, לא הותרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:14:1.english: We derive a matter that was not permitted from its general rule - Uncircumcision, in the context where [the Torah] forbade it — that is, regarding the Paschal offering — was not permitted:

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:14:2.english: From a matter that was not permitted from their general rule - [Improper intent regarding] time.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:1:1.hebrew: בהאי קרא פליגי - וכשיתכפרו בו ערלים דקאמר, שאין מנויין עליו קאמר, ומשום מחשבת שלא למנוייו קאמרי. אבל במנויין עליו, ושחטו למולים שהן נמי מנויין לזרוק דמו למנוייו ערלים שבהם לבדם — דהויא כולה זריקה לערלים מנוייו — דכולי עלמא פסול. ובערלים שאינן מנויין ומשום מחשבת שלא למנוייו פליגי. ובהאי קרא, דשלא למנוייו בזריקה מהכא נפיק בכל הקרבנות: "לכפר עליו" — היינו זריקה, "עליו" — ולא על הזורק לשם חבירו:
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:1:1.english: They disagree regarding this verse - And when it says "so that uncircumcised people may be atoned for by it," it is speaking of [uncircumcised people] who are not registered for it, and they are speaking about [disqualification due to] intent for non-registrants. However, where [uncircumcised people] are registered for it, and he slaughtered it for circumcised people who are also registered, [with the intent] to sprinkle its blood for its uncircumcised registrants alone — so that the entire sprinkling is for uncircumcised registrants — according to everyone it is disqualified. And they disagree regarding uncircumcised people who are not registered, and because of intent for non-registrants. And [they disagree] regarding this verse, for [the disqualification of] non-registrants at sprinkling is derived from here in all offerings: "to make atonement for him" — this refers to sprinkling; "for him" — and not for one who sprinkles on behalf of his fellow.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:1:2.hebrew: רבה סבר חבירו - דפסול משום שינוי בעלים, דומיא דידיה בעינן, מה הוא דבר כפרה כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:1:2.english: Rabbah holds [that] "his fellow" - [meaning] that [the offering] is disqualified on account of a change of owners — we require [that "his fellow" be] similar to him: "just as he is eligible for atonement," etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:2:1.english: He makes himself fit - He circumcises himself.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:4:1.hebrew: הואיל ואי מיקלעי ליה אורחים חזי ליה לא לקי - ואע"ג דאיהו השתא לא סעד ליה ולא צריך למידי:
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:4:1.english: Since if guests arrive it is fit for him, he is not flogged - Even though he himself is not dining now and does not need anything.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:5:1.hebrew: אלא דרב חסדא קשיא - השתא היכא דלא מחוסר מעשה — כגון זימון אורחים דלאו מעשה הוא — לית ליה הואיל, הכא, גבי ערל דמחוסר מעשה, אית ליה הואיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:5:1.english: But [that] of Rav Ḥisda is difficult - Now, where no action is lacking — such as inviting guests, which is not an action — he does not accept [the principle of] "since"; [yet] here, regarding an uncircumcised person, where an action is lacking, he does accept [the principle of] "since"?

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:5:2.english: To be lenient - To exempt him from lashes.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:5:3.english: To be stringent - To disqualify [it] in [the case of] Paschal offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:6:1.hebrew: בטומאת גברי - שנמנו עליו טמאים וטהורים, וכדפרישית לעיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 62a:6:1.english: With the ritual impurity of the people - That impure and pure [people] were registered for it [the Paschal lamb], and as I explained above.

Rashi on Pesachim 62a:6:2.english: The impure ones do not disqualify [them] - the Paschal offering for the pure ones.

Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:10:1.hebrew: ערל משלח קרבנות וטמא משלח כו' - כרבי עקיבא אתיא, דמרבי ערל כי טמא בחגיגה (דף ד:), דאי לאו הכי לייתי איהו גופיה קרבנותיו. וקשה לר"י: בריש חגיגה (שם) "טמא פטור מן הראייה, שנאמר: 'ובאת שמה והבאתם שמה' — כל שישנו בביאה ישנו בהבאה, וכל שאינו כו'", משמע דטמא אינו משלח שום קרבן, דבההוא קרא גופיה כתיבי שאר קרבנות: "עולותיכם וזבחיכם וגו'". ואומר ר"י, דמכל מקום דווקא בחגיגה שתלויה בביאה קפיד קרא, ואע"ג דכל הקרבנות כתיבי בקרא — לא קאי אכולהו, דהא מעשרות ותרומה כתיבי נמי התם. ועוד קשה לר"י: טמא איך משלח קרבנות? והא בעי סמיכה! ואפילו למאן דאמר ביאה במקצת לא שמה ביאה, ליכא למימר אפשר דמעייל ידיה וסמיך, דהא בפרק כל הפסולים (זבחים דף לג.) אמרינן: "כל הסומך — ראשו ורובו מכניס; מאי טעמא? כל כחו בעינן". ותירץ ר"י, דהכא מיירי בעופות — וכן משני בכל הגט (גיטין דף כח:) — אי נמי בבכור ומעשר, דלא בעי סמיכה, כדתנן פרק שתי מדות (מנחות דף צב:); ובקרבן נשים ליכא לאוקמי, משום ערל: [וע"ע תוס' יבמות קד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:10:1.english: An uncircumcised person sends offerings, and an impure person sends, etc. - This follows Rabbi Akiva, who includes an uncircumcised person like an impure person in Chagigah (4b), for if not so, he himself should bring his offerings. And R"i [Rabbi Yitzchak] raises a difficulty: In the beginning of Chagigah (ibid.), [it states:] "An impure person is exempt from appearing [with a pilgrimage offering], as it is stated: 'And you shall come there, and you shall bring there' — whoever is included in 'coming' is included in 'bringing,' and whoever is not [included in coming is not included in bringing], etc." This implies that an impure person does not send any offering, for in that very verse the other offerings are written: "your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, etc." And R"i says that nevertheless, the verse is only particular about the pilgrimage offering [chagigah], which depends on entering [the Temple]; and even though all the offerings are written in the verse, it does not refer to all of them, for tithes and terumah are also written there. And R"i raises another difficulty: How can an impure person send offerings? Why, it requires leaning [semikhah]! And even according to the one who says that partial entry is not considered entry, one cannot say that he can insert his hand and lean, for in the chapter Kol HaPesulim (Zevachim 33a), we say: "Anyone who performs leaning brings in his head and the majority of his body; what is the reason? We require all his strength." And R"i answered that here it is speaking of bird offerings — and so too [the Gemara] answers in [the chapter] Kol HaGet (Gittin 28b) — or else of a firstborn [animal] and [animal] tithe, which do not require leaning, as we learned in the Mishnah in the chapter Shtei Middot (Menachot 92b); and it is impossible to establish [the case] as referring to women's offerings, because of [the mention of] an uncircumcised person: [And see also Tosafot on Yevamot 104b

Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:5:1.hebrew: האי מחוסר מעשה כו' - הקשה ריב"א, דבפ' אלו עוברין (פסחים דף מז:) מסיק: "כתישה בי"ט מי שרי?" משמע, אי הוה שרי, אמרינן "הואיל", אע"ג דמחוסר מעשה. ותירץ ר"י, דהאי מעשה דמילה חשיב טפי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:5:1.english: This [case] is lacking an action, etc. - Riba raised a difficulty: for in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Overin (Pesachim 47b), [the Gemara] concludes: "Is pounding on a Festival permitted?" [This] implies [that] if it were permitted, we would say "since," even though it is lacking an action. And Ri answered that this action of circumcision is considered more significant.

Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:5:2.hebrew: כי לית ליה לקולא וכו' - נראה דרב חסדא לא פסל אלא מדרבנן, דמדאוריי' לא שייך לחלק בין לחומרא בין לקולא, ומדאוריי' לא אמרינן "הואיל" כלל, אפי' לחומרא. וכן מוכח בר"פ שני שעירים (יומא דס"ב:), דקאמר רבינא: "השתא דאמר ר"ח מחוסר הגרלה כמחוסר מעשה דמי" — פי': אם שחט שעיר יום הכפורים בחוץ היה פטור משום דמחוסר הגרלה, אי לאו משום דחזי לשעיר חיצון — "שלמים ששחטן קודם פתיחת ההיכל פטור, מחוסר פתיחה כמחוסר מעשה דמי". אלמא לית ליה "הואיל" אפילו לחומרא! ואין להקשות: אי מדרבנן, היאך יתחייב פסח אחר? הא קמייתי חולין לעזרה! לא היא: כיון דלא יזרוק הדם אינו יוצא, ומותר לצאת באחר. וכן מוכח בכיצד צולין, דאמר רב: "לא זרק את הדם חייב לעשות פסח אחר כו'". (תימה, דהשתא לרב אשי דמחשבת ערלים המנויין לכ"ע פסל אף בזריקה, וכשאינם מנויין איכא מאן דמכשר, וסברא משמע איפכא: דהשתא כשאינה מנויין לא פסלה, כ"ש במנויין):
Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:5:2.english: When he does not [accept it] to be lenient, etc. - It appears that Rav Chisda disqualified [the offering] only rabbinically, for by Torah law it is not appropriate to distinguish between stringency and leniency, and by Torah law we do not apply [the principle of] "since" at all, even for stringency. And so is proven at the beginning of the chapter Shnei Se'irim (Yoma 62b), where Ravina says: "Now that Rav Chisda said that lacking a lottery is like lacking an action" — meaning: if one slaughtered the Yom Kippur goat outside [the Temple], he would be exempt because it lacks a lottery, were it not that it is fit to be the outer goat — "[therefore,] peace-offerings that one slaughtered before the opening of the Sanctuary, he is exempt; lacking opening is like lacking an action." Thus [we see] he does not accept "since" even for stringency! And one should not object: If [it is disqualified only] rabbinically, how can he be obligated [to bring] another Pesach [offering]? Behold, he is bringing non-sacred [animals] into the Temple courtyard! That is not so: since he will not sprinkle the blood, he does not fulfill [his obligation], and it is permitted to fulfill [his obligation] with another [Pesach offering]. And so is proven in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin, where Rav says: "If he did not sprinkle the blood, he is obligated to make another Pesach [offering], etc." (This is astonishing, for now according to Rav Ashi, intent [for] uncircumcised people who are registered disqualifies according to all opinions even at the sprinkling, whereas when they are not registered there is one who declares it valid; yet logic implies the opposite: if when they are not registered it does not disqualify, all the more so when they are registered!):

Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:7:1.hebrew: מאי שנא טומאה דפשיטא ליה ומאי שנא ערלה דמספקא ליה - תימה לרשב"א: דלמא טומאה פשיטא ליה משום דילפינן טומאת גברי מטומאת בשר! וכי תימא דמשמע ליה דאי פשיטא לן בטומאת גברי דלא עשה בה מקצת טומאה ככל טומאה, הוא הדין בערלה, משום דמחד קרא ד"לפי אכלו" נפקי ותו לא הוה שייך למילף מזמן — מכל מקום, מאי קאמר "דנין דבר שלא הותר מכללו כו'"? הא ע"כ איכא למילף טפי טומאת גברי מטומאת בשר, דהוי טומאה מטומאה ודמי ליה בכל צד, מדנילף טומאת גברי מזמן דלא דמי ליה כלל; וכיון דפשיטא לן בטומאה דגברי, פשיטא לן נמי בערלה כיון שיש להשוותם, והיכי קבעי למילף ערלה מזמן? ואומר ר"י, דטומאת גברי נמי איכא למימר דנילף טפי מזמן מדנילף מטומאת בשר, משום דדנין פסול מחשבה מפסול מחשבה, ולא תוכיח טומאת בשר דלא הוי פסול מחשבה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 62a:7:1.english: What is different [about] impurity that it is obvious to him, and what is different [about] lack of circumcision that he is in doubt? - Rashba is puzzled: Perhaps impurity is obvious to him because we derive impurity of people from impurity of meat! And if you say that it seems to him that if it were obvious to us regarding impurity of people that partial impurity was not made like full impurity, the same [would apply] to lack of circumcision, because they are both derived from one verse, "according to his eating," and it would no longer be relevant to derive [it] from [intent for outside the] time — nevertheless, what does [the baraita] mean [when it says], "We derive a matter that was not permitted from its general rule, etc."? Behold, perforce we should rather derive impurity of people from impurity of meat — since it is [deriving] impurity from impurity and is similar to it in every respect — than derive impurity of people from [intent for outside the] time, which is not similar to it at all; and since it is obvious to us regarding impurity of people, it is also obvious to us regarding lack of circumcision since they are to be equated, so how could [the baraita] seek to derive lack of circumcision from [intent for outside the] time? And R. Yitzchak says that regarding impurity of people as well, one could say that we should rather derive [it] from [intent for outside the] time than derive [it] from impurity of meat, because we derive a disqualification of intention from a disqualification of intention, and impurity of meat should not prove [anything], since it is not a disqualification of intention.
